v4.9.082 - a picture is never replaced by nothing, and a field you are typing in stays open (#369, #370)

#369 NEVER THROW AWAY A PICTURE WE ALREADY HAVE.

     On every rebuild each picture was asked one question: does the copy I hold
     carry the same server name as the one up there? If yes it was kept. If not
     it was set to NOTHING and downloaded again.

     A photo just taken has no server name yet. A sync landing in that window
     therefore did not recognise the app's own picture, threw it away, and left
     the card empty until the download finished. Roman: "you take a photo and it
     takes quite a while till it appears as the version in the LOOKs... earlier
     it was immediately, which was much better."

     Whatever is held now stays on screen until something better arrives. The
     download is unchanged, so the right picture still lands exactly as before -
     the only difference is what you look at meanwhile. Replacing a picture with
     a picture is invisible; replacing it with nothing is not.

     Two lines: one for versions, one for main frames.

#370 DO NOT REBUILD A COLUMN SOMEBODY IS TYPING IN.

     Roman: "the categories in NEEDS when renamed sometimes just jump back in the
     middle of typing - the field closes and you stay there with half a name."

     Writing under a frame was always safe: the redraw copies the box into the
     frame before rebuilding anything. The little box you get when you click a
     category NAME never had that. It is made on the spot and destroyed by the
     next redraw, taking what was typed with it. The flash fix did not help and
     was never going to - it stopped pictures blanking, not redraws happening.

     Saving half a name would be worse than losing it, so the answer is not to
     save it but to leave that column alone while the cursor is in it. Everything
     else on the page still redraws; the column catches up the moment you click
     away. Applies to NEEDS and NOTES.

27 of 27 pass, twice, with the local server staying up both times.
